articles.headline: Anthony Gordon left Premier League for Barcelona to get 'respect' -- he's got it now
articles.description: Anthony Gordon's move to Barcelona was a surprise to some, but he's become an instant fan favorite at Camp Nou as well as a key player for England.
articles.headlineJa: アンソニー・ゴードンが「尊敬」を求めてプレミアリーグを離れバルセロナへ――そして今、彼はそれを手に入れた
articles.descriptionJa: アンソニー・ゴードンのバルセロナ移籍は一部で驚きを持って迎えられたが、彼はすぐにカンプ・ノウのファンに愛される存在となり、イングランド代表の鍵を握る選手となった。
articles.body:
As a child living in Merseyside, Anthony Gordon envisaged playing for Barcelona. That in itself is no different to many youngsters growing up around the world, but you get the feeling he always believed he would make it happen -- and he did.

Gordon has hit the ground running at Barça, ever since he signed from Newcastle United for an initial €70 million in the summer. The England winger is already a fixture of coach Hansi Flick's preferred attack, alongside Lamine Yamal and Raphinha, and there was no doubt he would start Tuesday's UEFA Champions League win against Aston Villa or Sunday's top-of-the-table clash against Atlético Madrid in LaLiga (watch live on ESPN+ at 3 p.m. ET).

Gordon's path to this stage of his career has included relegation battles with boyhood club Everton, a loan spell with Preston North End in 2021, and scoreless streaks with Newcastle after he moved there in 2023. But he never blinkered from his belief that he was destined for the top level. Others are now seeing what he has always felt.

- Yamal makes history as ruthless Barça end Villa's perfect UCL start

- Why LaLiga's top stars Yamal and Mbappé didn't deserve Ballon d'Or

- Global power ranking: The top 20 soccer teams in the world, ranked!

Earlier this season, the 25-year-old spoke about people in England beginning to respect "the quality and IQ that I play with." His comments were interpreted as an indication he had not always received the recognition he deserved in his homeland. Speaking to ESPN earlier this week, he clarified those remarks were not meant as a negative, but to underline that he has now found a home to really exhibit his talent. 

"I didn't mean people were judging me wrong or had a negative perspective of me," he said. "I meant they had never seen me in a system that highlights these qualities. People hadn't seen me in this kind of system before, which I think is helping them appreciate me more."

Did he have to leave the Premier League to make that happen? -- Sam Marsden

Premier League progression: 'I'm not surprised he's at Barça now'

In the away changing room after Burnley lost 2-1 at St. James' Park last season, Maxime Estève talked to his teammates about Gordon. The defender, now at RB Leipzig, tells ESPN: "I told them 'this guy is really good, really sharp, has a really good right foot, great at one vs. ones.' I like that type of winger: they want to beat the right back each time, and even if they lose the ball four times, you know they're going to pass you two times and cause danger." Gordon had certainly earnt Estève's respect.

Gordon's time at Newcastle wasn't always entirely plain sailing. There were untimely niggles and frustration, like the clash he had with manager Eddie Howe after being brought on and then substituted against Brentford late in the 2022-23 season. articles.headline: Does Man United's coach matter? Could Jurgen Klopp reach Premier League glory at Old Trafford?
articles.description: If Manchester United hired an all-time great like Jurgen Klopp, would they have won the Premier League? Let's find out!
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドの監督は重要か？ユルゲン・クロップならオールド・トラッフォードでプレミアリーグ制覇を果たせたか？
articles.descriptionJa: もしマンチェスター・ユナイテッドがユルゲン・クロップのような史上最高の指導者を雇っていたら、プレミアリーグで優勝できていたのだろうか？検証してみよう。
articles.body:
Right around this time every year, you can start to feel it. The air gets a little crisper. The shadows get a little colder. The days get shorter. The tree colors start to pop. You start wearing sweaters. Pumpkins appear in places where they do and do not belong.

Everyone and everything starts to shift, just slightly, in preparation for what's about to happen. The cycles of nature can be fickle and unpredictable, so the date is never exactly the same, and some years come and go without anything at all. But most years, it does.

Our tiny little rituals prime us to anticipate the inevitable, oncoming shift: that moment when Manchester United fire their manager and convince themselves that the new guy is finally going to be the one who fixes everything.

Ruben Amorim lost his job last January. Erik ten Hag was fired two years ago, right before Halloween. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer got the boot just a couple days before Thanksgiving. And Jose Mourinho was relieved of his duties a little over a week before Christmas.

Now that we've once again entered the season of sacking, Michael Carrick seems like he will inevitably become the latest victim.

Man United are clear of the relegation zone on goal differential alone. If history is any indication, their comeback against AS Roma in the Champions League will end up being meaningless. Before Tuesday's win, Carrick appeared to be on the verge of tears at the end of every match.

This is the 14th season since Manchester United last won the Premier League. And whoever replaces Carrick will be the ninth coach to try and do something that no other United manager since has done: just, simply, meet the expectations at one of the richest sports teams on the planet for more than a single season in a row.

But given how many different coaches have now failed since Sir Alex Ferguson left the club, it makes you wonder: Could anyone have been successful at Manchester United?

What is a great manager worth?

Arsenal won the Premier League last season with 85 points.

If we lived in a world where there were no subs and everyone on the field contributed exactly evenly to their team's success, then all 11 Arsenal players would have contributed about 8 points (7.7, to be slightly more exact) of value last season.

Except, the alternative to each player isn't just zero points. If you removed Bukayo Saka from the lineup, you wouldn't have to play a man down. No, you'd get to put another player out there who would also contribute to winning to some degree.

So, let's look at the relegation-level cut-off. West Ham were relegated with 39 points. Using the same framework, we'd say that all of their players were worth a little over 3.5 points across the season. We could then say that the average Arsenal player provided 5 more points of value than a relegation-level player.

articles.headline: Forget about Cowboys' D, what happened to the GOTI offense?
articles.description: This summer, they talked about having the Greatest Offense There Is, but it's been worse than 2025.
articles.headlineJa: カウボーイズの守備はさておき、「史上最強(GOTI)」の攻撃陣に何が起きたのか？
articles.descriptionJa: 今夏の彼らは「史上最強の攻撃陣(Greatest Offense There Is)」を掲げていたが、実際には2025年よりもひどい状況となっている。
articles.body:
FRISCO, Texas -- For all of the issues surrounding the Dallas Cowboys' defense in 2026 -- and there are many -- there is a more perplexing reason why they are 3-5: a star-laden offense that returned every starter from a unit that was among the NFL's best in 2025.

The points per game remain about the same (27.4 in 2026; 27.7 in 2025) and some areas are actually better this season (third-down rate, red zone offense), but the offense is putting up 50 less yards per game (391.9 to 342). The running game is off by 31 yards (125.6 to 94.1). The passing output has dipped from 266.3 yards per game to 247.9.

Pass plays of 20 yards or more are down from 3.3 per game to 2.6. Runs of 10 yards or more are down from 2.7 per game to 1.8.

In the first eight games last year, receiver George Pickens had 43 catches for 685 yards and six touchdowns. In the first eight this year, he has 39 for 533 yards and two scores. Tight end Jake Ferguson had 51 receptions for 334 yards and six scores in the first eight games of 2025. He has 17 for 115 yards and three touchdowns this year, and he is now battling an ankle injury.

On his way to 1,200 rushing yards in 2025, Javonte Williams had more than 75 rushing yards in five of his first eight games. He has two such games in the first eight this year, although he has matched the eight rushing touchdowns from that stretch in 2025.

Quarterback Dak Prescott had a completion percentage of 65.5% or better in six of the first eight games last season. This year, it's three of eight.

During the summer, Prescott talked about an offense that would be GOTI, an acronym for Greatest Offense There Is. He was asked Thursday if the Cowboys have found an offensive identity. He paused for a few seconds.

"Yeah, sure," he said. "I mean, is it one we're proud of? I don't know. We'll be better, I can promise you."

Speaking on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas on Tuesday, owner and general manager Jerry Jones used the word "rebuild" when talking about the defense with first-time coordinator Christian Parker and a changeover in personnel through free agency and the draft.

"We had a letdown there in the game Sunday," Jones told the team's flagship station in reference to last week's 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals. "The plan is dependent upon that offense carrying us when we have weakness in the defense as we evolve going forward."

The Cowboys have scored at least 30 points five times, but when they have been needed most -- at the end of the Baltimore Ravens loss in Rio de Janeiro in Week 3, in the fourth quarter and overtime against the Cardinals, for largely the entirety of the losses to the Green Bay Packers and Tampa Bay Buccaneers -- they have not had answers.

"It's hard to say we're pressing, but yeah, when you've got the talent we've got, when you've got the expectation, the standards that we have for ourselves and you go three-and-out or you don't score a touchdown, yeah, that's frustrating and you've got to make sure that you don'

articles.headline: Dolphins coach Hafley brings familiarity with Lions
articles.description: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley saw plenty of the Lions' top-ranked offense while leading Packers defense.
articles.headlineJa: ドルフィンズのハフレイ監督、ライオンズへの熟知した知見を注入
articles.descriptionJa: ジェフ・ハフレイ・ドルフィンズ監督は、パッカーズの守備を率いていた際、リーグトップの攻撃力を誇るライオンズを数多く分析してきた。
articles.body:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- Jeff Hafley knows what to expect when it comes to facing the Detroit Lions.

The Miami Dolphins coach spent two years preparing for Detroit as the Green Bay Packers' defensive coordinator; when asked about the challenges Detroit presents, he had to stop himself after a lengthy, detailed answer about stars such as Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Sam LaPorta.

Ahead of their matchup with the Lions on Sunday (1 p.m., E.T., CBS), the Dolphins' gameplan is rooted in respect for the NFL's top-ranked offense.

"I think they're built the right way and they're the No. 1 offense in the NFL for a reason," Hafley said. "It's coaching, it's players, it's developing. Give coach (Dan Campbell) credit and give them credit, he's done a great job."

The Lions average 395 yards per game this season, while their 29 points per game ranks third in the league. Gibbs and St. Brown rank second and 10th in rushing and receiving yards, respectively, and Goff has thrown only one interception against 15 touchdowns.

Similar to when the Dolphins faced the 49ers in Week 2, Hafley said Sunday's game presents an "exciting" challenge for the youngest defense in the NFL.

"They could hit you from a variety of different angles, whether it's in the run game or the pass game," he said. "I view that as a challenge that we look forward to. I mean, anytime you get a chance to go up against the top offense in the league, you need to prepare and you need to rise up to the level that you're going to play against. And for a young group of guys, I think it's really exciting."

The Lions rank third in the NFL in explosive plays -- rushes of at least 10 yards and completions of at least 20 yards. Miami hopes to limit such plays by controlling time of possession and keeping the Lions' offense off the field.

Rookie left guard Kadyn Proctor is trending toward playing Sunday after missing last week's game with a concussion. He practiced fully twice by the end of the week.

Proctor was missed in Week 8; the Dolphins entered the week averaging 3.09 yards before contact per rush attempt, the second-most in the NFL. In last week's loss to the Patriots, however, they averaged a season-low 1.74 yards before contact.

Running back Ollie Gordon II said Proctor's presence will be felt.

"It's one of those things that I feel like once you've been in so many weeks with certain people, it's just boom, you mesh," Gordon said. "You mesh different, so I feel like it's one of those things we'll get back to it. It'll be us, and we'll be back to being us."

Sunday also presents an intriguing stage for the Dolphins' fledgling passing offense, which ranks 30th in yards per game this season. Detroit allows a league-high 276.6 passing yards per game, but Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis isn't ready to call Sunday an advantageous matchup.

articles.headline: Packers give Micah Parsons boost in return from ACL injury
articles.description: Green Bay hopes Parsons will be back before Thanksgiving as it remains in the playoff hunt.
articles.headlineJa: パッカーズ、ACL（前十字靭帯）負傷から復帰するマイカ・パーソンズへの期待が高まる
articles.descriptionJa: プレーオフ進出を争うグリーンベイは、パーソンズが感謝祭までに復帰することを期待している。
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- In the back of their minds, those in the Green Bay Packers' locker room knew Micah Parsons' return at some point this season would matter only if they did one thing: Stay alive.

Three weeks into the season, there was reason to think that wouldn't happen. The Packers were 1-2, and the return of their star pass rusher was still weeks, even months, away.

Yet safety Xavier McKinney, one of the defensive captains, had one thought.

"Get back into the mix," he said, "and let's get this thing going."

By the time Parsons returned to the practice field Wednesday, the Packers had done just that. At 5-3 heading into Sunday's game at the New England Patriots (4:25 p.m. ET, Fox), they're smack dab in the NFC playoff picture nearing the midway point of the season. While Parsons is expected to miss at least two more games with an eye on returning for the Thanksgiving Eve game at the Los Angeles Rams, the Packers believe they've given Parsons a reason to come back for something more than just individual pride after a devastating and complex knee injury.

"We put ourselves in a solid situation," McKinney said. "It could be better, and we all know that. But it could be worse."

Parsons didn't necessarily look at the season that way. He was coming back, eventually, regardless of the Packers' record when he was cleared to return. He was focused on the end of the season, not the beginning, especially after they began last season 9-3-1 before losing five straight after he blew out his knee in Week 15.

"I don't really buy into records because you've seen teams that lose a lot of games, finish strong, or last year we started strong, finished terrible," Parsons said after his return to practice on Wednesday. "It doesn't really matter about how you start, it's about how you finish."

That's exactly the conversation Parsons said he was having recently with rookie edge rusher Dani Dennis-Sutton, who, like Parsons, played at Penn State before coming to the NFL.

"I said, 'It's November time. You've got to lock in,'" Parsons said.

Dennis-Sutton asked, "What's November time?"

"I said, 'I get it, you're at Penn State last year, you're getting ready to think about bowl game you're heading to,'" Parsons said. "But I said, 'November gets ready for December, and December tells us who we're going to be for playoffs. ... It's going to get harder, it's going to be more challenging, but we've got to be ready to step up.'

"That's what I'm excited for. I came back for the greatest time of football, and that's November football and December football. Let the show begin."

In some ways, the Packers' defense has overachieved without Parsons. Through Week 8, the Packers ranked in the top 10 in fewest yards allowed (10th), fewest passing yards allowed (eighth) and fewest points allowed (10th).

They have allowed 20 or fewer points in five straight games, their longest single-season streak since 2022 and one short of their longest streak since they won the Super Bowl

articles.headline: What turned around Washington's defense?
articles.description: Safety NIck Cross and LB Dorance Armstrong missed time but are beginning to jell with the new pass rushers.
articles.headlineJa: ワシントンのディフェンスを好転させた要因は？
articles.descriptionJa: セーフティのニック・クロスとLBのドランス・アームストロングは欠場していたが、新たなパスラッシャーたちと連携し始めている。
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- Midway through the first quarter Sunday, the Washington Commanders ' offseason vision for its pass rush came to light. They showed seven defenders at the line of scrimmage; both inside linebackers stood at the line on either side of the center.

Then came the organized chaos and, for Washington, the fun. And a blueprint for what the Commanders (2-4-1) need to compensate for losing its top two defensive linemen, if it wants to turn its season around -- starting Sunday vs. the Rams (4-4).

After all, they spent nearly $100 million in guaranteed money in the offseason to help the pass rush. It needs to help lead any resurgence and that was the case in Week 8.

"It was definitely a snapshot of what we can be," Washington defensive coordinator Daronte Jones said. "Now it's just about consistency."

If they find it, it would provide a big boost -- especially with linemen Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw both out for the season.

"The better we are," outside linebacker Dorance Armstrong said of the pass rush, "the better our defense is. Everyone knows that."

Numerous plays showed their ability to pressure the passer. But this third-down play vs. the Eagles in Week 8 showed what can happen when they work more together, as Jones and coach Dan Quinn have wanted.

At the snap on this third-and-6, inside linebacker Sonny Styles dropped into coverage as did Armstrong. The edge rusher on the right side, K'Lavon Chaisson, stepped forward, drew the attention of the left tackle, then looped inside with tackle Charles Omenihu moving outside.

That's all safety Nick Cross needed for a free rush off the edge, and that forced Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee to throw a deep out early and the pass fell 5 yards from its intended target.

It was coordinated. It was effective. It didn't result in a huge play, but it incorporated what they had hoped. And it wasn't the only time this happened in that 27-10 win; they pressured McKee on a season-high 46.5% of dropbacks.

"Last week gives you a snapshot of when guy are working in unison, whether it's a four-man or five-man [rush]," Jones said, "you never know who's going to make the play or who may come to life. As long as we're doing those things consistently there's some shining light to be seen."

The trick will be incorporating this level of pressure vs. the Rams' Matthew Stafford, one of the hardest quarterbacks to harass. He ranks fourth in terms of pressure rate and eighth in the league in quickest release. He's also thrown 80 play-action passes, another way to try to slow the pass rush.

"It's all about the rush in the middle of the pocket," Chaisson said. "It's about getting hands in the face, making him uncomfortable, making it muddy and getting the offensive linemen to step on his toes, hit him on his follow through, anything you can do to disrupt the timing and rhythm."

Finally, teams pressure him on only 37.6% of their blitzes -- the fourth-lowest rate in the league.

articles.headline: How the Jets trading stars Quinnen Williams and Sauce Gardner looks a year later
articles.description: Hours before the 2025 trade deadline, New York stockpiled first-round picks by sending its two stars to the Colts and Cowboys.
articles.headlineJa: ジェッツがスターのクインン・ウィリアムズとソース・ガードナーをトレードして1年、その結果は
articles.descriptionJa: 2025年のトレード期限の数時間前、ニューヨークは2人のスター選手をコルツとカウボーイズに放出することで、1巡目指名権を大量に確保した。
articles.body:
In less time than it takes to play an NFL game, the New York Jets made two blockbuster trades ahead of the 4 p.m. ET deadline on Nov. 4, 2025, that would help alter the trajectory of three franchises.

First, it was cornerback Sauce Gardner being traded to the Indianapolis Colts, first reported at 12:47 p.m. Then, it was defensive tackle Quinnen Williams being sent to the Dallas Cowboys at 2:05 p.m. The impact of the deals has already contributed to significant aftershocks.

Since then, the combined record of the three teams is 14-35.

The Colts' architect, general manager Chris Ballard, was fired Oct. 19.

Two coaches, the Jets' Aaron Glenn and the Colts' Shane Steichen, are fighting for their jobs, having gone 4-13 and 3-13, respectively.

Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer, too, could be in trouble if his team doesn't challenge in a watered-down NFC East.

A quick refresher:

For the 25-year-old Gardner, a top young cornerback, the Jets received first-round picks in 2026 and 2027, along with wide receiver Adonai Mitchell -- widely perceived as a "throw-in" player, but New York insisted that he be included in the package.

For Williams, one of the league's best defensive tackles, the Jets landed a 2026 second-round pick, a 2027 first-round pick and defensive tackle Mazi Smith, whom they cut in training camp. They have the rights to the better of the Cowboys' two first-round picks in 2027, as Dallas has its own selection and the Green Bay Packers' pick from the Micah Parsons trade. The Jets insisted on that during negotiations.

"I don't know if I would've traded two star defensive players in their prime," said a former NFC GM who is a current personnel analyst. "In hindsight, it worked out pretty well. The next guy will walk into a nice situation" -- meaning he assumes Glenn won't be back in 2027.

The Jets, who accepted short-term pain for long-term gain, still are waiting to reap the full benefits of the trades. That will come in April, when they enter the draft with three first-round picks. With a glaring need at quarterback, they could have the ammo to target a specific player -- one of the main reasons for last year's trades.

Coming into Week 9, ESPN Analytics projects them to have the fifth (their own), sixth (Colts) and 14th (Cowboys) selections. The Colts, who recently traded guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner for draft capital, are sinking like a horseshoe in a swimming pool, so that pick could be in the top three or four.

"For the Jets, the Sauce Gardner trade might be one of the best of all time because of the draft compensation, and then you add in Mitchell, who can be a strong receiver," an AFC personnel scout said. "On the other hand, it has to be among the worst trades in Colts history because of the collapse."

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal tracking RB Leipzig's Nusa after Vinicius snub
articles.description: RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa is being tracked by Arsenal ahead of the January transfer window. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.headlineJa: 移籍の噂・ニュース：アーセナル、ヴィニシウス獲得断念後にRBライプツィヒのヌサを追跡
articles.descriptionJa: 1月の移籍市場を前に、RBライプツィヒのウィング、アントニオ・ヌサがアーセナルの監視対象となっている。Transfer Talkが最新情報を伝える。
articles.body:
Arsenal are now eyeing RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa after Real Madrid's Vinícius Júnior turned them down last summer, while Newcastle United could compete with Manchester United for Al Ahli striker Ivan Toney. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa is being tracked by Arsenal ahead of the January transfer window, according to The Sun. Nusa, 21, has 16 goals and 18 assists from 85 games at Leipzig and could slot into the left wing slot left open at the Emirates by the exits of Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard, after Real Madrid's Vinícius Júnior turned them down last summer. However, Leipzig don't need to raise any funds as they let Yan Diomande move to Real Madrid for €125 million last window, so will look to keep the Norway international even if a bid of €60 million arrives.

- Newcastle United are considering a January move for Al Ahli striker Ivan Toney, as per Football Insider. The 30-year-old has previously worked with Magpies head coach Matthias Jaissle in the Saudi Pro League, which could potentially help get a deal over the line. Manchester United have also shortlisted Toney as they assess options to strengthen their attack following Benjamin Šeško's injury.

- Arsenal and Manchester United are monitoring AFC Bournemouth midfielder Marcus Tavernier, according to TEAMtalk. The Gunners have been compiling scouting reports on the 27-year-old as they assess options to strengthen their attack, while they also admire his teammate Junior Kroupi. Tavernier, who has scored six goals in 14 appearances this season, is also attracting interest from Newcastle and long-time admirers Tottenham Hotspur.

- Bayern Munich are considering signing FC Porto winger Oskar Pietuszewski as a backup for Luis Díaz next summer, Sky Germany reports. The 18-year-old has a €60 million release clause in his contract, with Bayern already informed of the details and discussions having taken place. Porto sporting director Max Eberl is a big fan of Pietuszewski, who has been capped six times by Poland since making his international debut at the beginning of the year.

- Arsenal and Manchester City are monitoring Newcastle United full back Tino Livramento, Football Insider has revealed. Both clubs are longstanding admirers of the 23-year-old and have previously seen attempts to sign him blocked by Newcastle. However, the Premier League club could reluctantly sanction his exit next summer if they can't make progress on a new contract, with Livramento's current deal due to expire in 2028.

- Tottenham Hotspur retain first-option matching rights on Harry Kane despite his new Bayern Munich contract running until 2029, according to The Telegraph. articles.headline: Fantasy football 10-team Knockout league rankings: The 126 players to draft
articles.description: Rankings for knockout leagues, where the lowest-scoring team is eliminated and the last team standing wins.
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジーフットボール 10チーム制ノックアウトリーグ・ランキング：指名すべき126人の選手
articles.descriptionJa: 最低得点のチームが脱落し、最後に勝ち残ったチームが優勝するノックアウトリーグ向けのランキング。
articles.body:
Tristan H. Cockcroft's 2026 fantasy football Knockout league rankings will be updated throughout the season to reflect the latest news, trends and opinions. Use them to inform your own rankings, or as a guide to draft your team. Sign up for your team for free.

Knockout leagues are our newest offering for 2026, challenging fantasy football managers to avoid being the last-place scorer in any given week, with the final team standing winning the championship. For those new to the format, here's a strategy primer to help you fine-tune your game.

The rankings below will differ slightly from our standard offering in that Knockout leagues begin with 18 teams, creating more demand at thinner positions such as quarterback and tight end. Additionally, week-over-week consistency carries additional weight, players with injury or other availability concerns are less desirable, and later-year bye weeks can prove advantageous. A standard 18-team knockout league comprises 14 slots including a kicker and a defense, so the rankings began 252 deep at season's start, and are now 126 deep (9 teams times 14 players) for leagues drafting to begin in Week 10, to take you from the first overall selection through to the final pick of the draft.

Remember that if you want to start a league that plays this week your draft must be completed by the time players lock for Thursday Night Football, otherwise your league will begin play the following week.  An 10-team league lets you eliminate nine players through Week 17, leaving only the winner standing.

articles.headline: 'No excuses': Ruben Amorim slams team, questions himself after shock Milan loss
articles.description: AC Milan coach Ruben Amorim questioned himself and hit out at his team after a shock 2-0 home loss to Hungarian side Ferencvaros on Thursday.
articles.headlineJa: 「言い訳は無用」：ルベン・アモリム、ミランの衝撃的な敗戦後にチームを猛批判し自問
articles.descriptionJa: ACミランのルベン・アモリム監督は木曜日、ハンガリーのフェレンツヴァーロシュにホームで2-0という衝撃的な敗戦を喫した後、自らの采配を疑い、チームを厳しく批判した。
articles.body:
AC Milan coach Ruben Amorim questioned himself and hit out at his team as not mentally prepared after their Europa League prospects were left in peril by a shock 2-0 home loss to Hungarian side Ferencvaros on Thursday.

Amorim's side were looking to build on their victory over Serie A rivals Inter Milan on Saturday but produced another lackluster European display.

- Tyler Adams' 1st goal in a year helps Bournemouth stay perfect in Europa

- Pulisic, Balogun, McKennie return to USMNT for Nations League QF vs. Haiti

Lenny Joseph scored twice as Ferencvaros pulled off a major upset at San Siro to extend their perfect start to the league phase, despite a late red card for substitute Bamidele Yusuf, to leave Milan with just three points from four games and down in 28th place.

"When you play for Milan, you have a responsibility," Amorim said. "You can't go out there like this. We're not ready to compete on both fronts in Serie A and Europe. We need to work on our approach to matches.

"There's nothing I can say, we had to win. It was an important match. I can't say anything to defend the team."

While Milan have made a promising start in Serie A, losing just once in 10 games, they have suffered defeat in three of their four matches in Europe's secondary competition.  

"Maybe I did something wrong in the last few days," former Manchester United manager Amorim added. "Last year the team had similar problems and today we weren't ready, we didn't have the attitude to try to come back at all costs if behind. Tonight we have no excuses."

Amorim made six changes from the lineup that beat Inter at the weekend before making a triple substitution at halftime, including bringing on United States star Christian Pulisic.

After the visitors put Milan's defense under pressure in the first half, Joseph struck twice for them in a span of 14 minutes early after the break.

The forward capitalized on a mistake by backup goalkeeper Lorenzo Torriani to net the opener and added his second on fast counter amid Milan's effort to equalize.

Milan failed to use a one-man advantage after Ferencvaros substitute Yusuf received a straight red in the 77th minute.

"They were better technically, tactically, and especially mentally, they deserved to win," Amorim said. "We were not prepared to play professional football today."

"We need to look at ourselves and to be better."

The Associated Press and PA contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Tyler Adams: Bournemouth have 'turned a page' after seventh straight win
articles.description: United States midfielder Tyler Adams has said his Bournemouth side have "turned a page" after a 3-1 Europa League win over Sparta Prague on Thursday.
articles.headlineJa: タイラー・アダムス：ボーンマスは7連勝を飾り「新たな局面を迎えた」
articles.descriptionJa: アメリカ代表MFのタイラー・アダムスは、木曜日のヨーロッパリーグでスパルタ・プラハに3-1で勝利した後、自身の所属するボーンマスは「新たな局面を迎えた」と語った。
articles.body:
United States captain Tyler Adams has said his Bournemouth side have "turned a page" after a 3-1 Europa League win over Sparta Prague on Thursday.

Adams struck in the 57th minute to level the game, after which Rayan and Evanilson both scored to seal the points.

Bournemouth have now won their last seven matches in all competitions.

"We can't get too comfortable," Adams said to TNT. "You have to be able to hold that winning standard, that winning mentality becomes contagious, especially when you are playing every three days.

"It doesn't feel that long ago since we lost 5-1 to Chelsea and that stings a little bit, we don't want to feel that ever again.

"I think we turned a page and we have been a more mature team ever since that -- the way that we defend, the way that we take pride in the mentality of making sure we don't give the opposition any opportunity to breathe.

"Everyone is working hard every day in training. Guys that aren't playing are working hard, the guys that are playing are working hard, so there's a lot of competition, but that breeds success. I'm happy with the team's performance."

Adams hailed Evanilson, 27, who stuck a brilliant finish across the goalkeeper into the corner in the 81st minute to put his team in front in the Czech capital.

It maintained their perfect start in the Europa League with four wins from four, leaving them in a strong position to progress directly into the last 16.

"[Evanilson] is on fire right now," Adams added.

"You see him work on it in training, he does extra work on his finishing every day after training so for him to do it in a game is no surprise.

- Ogden: Ronaldo's Portugal career ended in shame, but at his peak he was a dominant force

- Tighe: Run, Man United, run: How preseason fitness can hinder Premier League form

- Harry Kane signs new Bayern Munich contract: 'I want to win many more titles'

"He has so much quality, so whenever he gets in and around the box we are confident that is going to find the back of the net."

Bournemouth were awarded a first-half penalty for handball, but Lewis Cook's kick struck the post.

Sparta then went ahead via a brilliant individual goal from Gambian forward Ebrima Singhateh.

Tobias Guddal let his team down badly when he picked up a second yellow card within two minutes of his side taking the lead.

The visitors made the extra man count and equalised just before the hour mark.

Álvaro Rodríguez found his path to goal blocked on the edge of the box, but Sparta were unable fully to clear, the ball breaking to Adams, who rifled it first time into the bottom corner.

Bournemouth were soon well on top and deserved their winning goal.

Adrien Truffert won the ball on the edge of the area, Ryan Christie took over and slipped in Evanilson, who showed wonderful feet to make space and finish into the far corner.

Rayan drilled in a third from range in the last minute.

Information from PA contributed to this report.

articles.body:
Manchester City left back Rayan Aït-Nouri could join rivals Manchester United, while Como center back Jacobo Ramón has caught the eye of Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal and Liverpool. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester City left back Rayan Aït-Nouri could join rivals Manchester United, as he is seeking an exit in January, according to The Sun. Ait-Nouri, 25, has played only four times this season and has yet to appear in the Premier League. United are looking for a long-term replacement for Luke Shaw, and have been linked with Newcastle United's Lewis Hall, AFC Bournemouth's Adrien Truffert and Barcelona's Alejandro Balde, but could turn to the Algeria international.

- Manchester United are one of several clubs keen on signing Como center back Jacobo Ramón, TEAMtalk reports. The 21-year-old, who transfer is valued at around €50 million, impressed the Red Devils during Como's 4-1 UEFA Champions League victory over them last month. Chelsea are also keen, while Arsenal, Liverpool and Fulham are monitoring his development in Italy. However, his former club Real Madrid are considering exercising their option to re-sign him next summer, potentially complicating any move from Premier League clubs.

- Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United have stepped up their scouting of Galatasaray attacking midfielder Alexsey Batrakov, according to TEAMtalk. All three clubs watched the 21-year-old score twice against Stuttgart on Tuesday evening in the UEFA Champions League. The Russia international is reported to have a release clause worth €60 million, although a January departure is considered unlikely as Gala are looking to open talks over an improved contract and could seek to remove the clause as part of any new agreement.

- Everton are interested in signing Palmeiras striker Vitor Roque in 2027, as per Diario Sport. The Brazilian club are unwilling to open negotiations at less than €50 million for the 21-year-old, whose contract runs until December 2029. A move could also provide a windfall for his former club Barcelona, who retained 20% of his economic rights after his move to Palmeiras last year and would receive €10 million from a transfer at that price. Roque has scored five goals in 19 league matches this season.

- Liverpool are in advanced talks with 19-year-old midfielder Trey Nyoni over a contract extension, according to The Athletic. Discussions have been ongoing for several months, with all parties optimistic that an agreement will be reached, although nothing has been finalized. Nyoni has more than 3½ years remaining on his current deal, but Liverpool want to reward his progress under Andoni Iraola. The club rejected a £30 million offer from Nottingham Forest to sign him in the summer.
